title: Container Image Update Backlog
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=docker:stats
| stats latest(image_age_days) as age_days, latest(update_available) as update_available by container_name

description: Lists self-hosted containers running old images with an update available, so security patches do not pile up unnoticed.
value: Self-hosted apps miss the auto-updates cloud services get; a staleness list keeps your exposure low without a full patch-management tool.
implementation: Forward image age and update-availability data; schedule weekly and review the update backlog.
visualization: Table of containers by image age with an update flag.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Docker — Docker stats via telegraf or scripted input on host → HEC.
• **Subcategory context**: Home Lab & Self-Hosting — typical feeds: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `docker:stats`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Docker** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=docker:stats`.

**Collection method:** Docker stats via telegraf or scripted input on host → HEC.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `docker stats --no-stream JSON`.

**Suggested poll interval:** 60s.

**Key fields to extract:** `container_name, cpu_percent, mem_usage, mem_limit`.

**Typical connector stack:** Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC..

**Author notes:** Forward image age and update-availability data; schedule weekly and review the update backlog.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "docker:stats", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=docker:stats earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Container Image Update Backlog** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=docker:stats`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `age_days` (> 30) after latest — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `age_days`, `container_name`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=docker:stats
| stats latest(image_age_days) as age_days, latest(update_available) as update_available by container_name
| where update_available="true" AND age_days>30
| sort - age_days
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Portainer or `docker stats` on the host. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=docker:stats earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table age_days, container_name
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=docker:stats earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `age_days` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=docker:stats earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(age_days) AS p50 perc90(age_days) AS p90 perc99(age_days) AS p99 max(age_days) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.8.9: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Of Containers By Image Age With An Update Flag (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Docker — no Docker events / missing fields:** If `docker:stats` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Docker connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Docker — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Docker JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=docker:stats | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Docker — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Docker — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Docker APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
